reprBidict(entries in insertion order):
  "bidict({" + entries.map(([k,v]) => pyReprStr(k) + ": " + pyIntStr(v)).join(", ") + "})"
  - separator is exactly comma+space ", "
  - after the colon exactly ONE space; NO space before the colon
  - NO trailing comma, ever. 1 entry -> bidict({'k': 1}); 2 -> bidict({'a': 1, 'b': 2}); an empty bidict is unreachable here.
  - order = insertion order of first assignment of each key; re-assigning an existing key keeps its original slot.
  - no wrapping/truncation at any length.

pyIntStr(v): canonical decimal of an arbitrary-precision integer. Use BigInt in Node (values like 123456789012345678901234567890 occur). Format: optional '-' then digits, no '+', no grouping, "-0" -> "0". Argparse's int() accepts optional surrounding ASCII whitespace, optional +/-, underscores between digits, and leading zeros; it rejects 0x/0o/0b prefixes, floats, and empty/garbage (rc=2 argparse error).

pyReprStr(s) — Python 3 str repr, operating on UNICODE CODE POINTS (not UTF-16 units; iterate with [...s] / codePointAt in Node):
  1) Quote choice: if s contains "'" AND does not contain '"'  -> quote = '"' ; otherwise quote = "'".
  2) Emit quote, then for each code point cp:
       - cp === 0x5C (backslash)            -> "\\\\"   (two backslashes)
       - cp === code of the chosen quote     -> "\\" + that quote   (only the delimiter is escaped; the other quote char is emitted raw. '"' is NEVER escaped when the delimiter is "'", and "'" is NEVER escaped when the delimiter is '"')
       - cp === 0x0A -> "\\n" ; cp === 0x0D -> "\\r" ; cp === 0x09 -> "\\t"   (these are the ONLY short escapes; \a \b \f \v \0 do NOT exist)
       - else if isPrintable(cp) is false:
             cp <= 0xFF      -> "\\x" + hex2(cp)          e.g. \x07 \x1b \x7f \x85 \xa0 \xad
             cp <= 0xFFFF    -> "\\u" + hex4(cp)          e.g. ​       　 ᠎ ؜ ͸  ﻿ ￾ ﷐ \udcff
             else            -> "\\U" + hex8(cp)          e.g. \U0010ffff \U000e0001 \U000f0000 \U0001fffe
             hex digits are LOWERCASE, zero-padded to exactly 2/4/8.
       - else emit the code point raw (UTF-8 on the wire).
     then emit the closing quote.
  3) isPrintable(cp): FALSE iff cp === 0x20 ? no—0x20 IS printable. Precisely: printable = NOT (Unicode general category is one of Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, Zs) — with the single exception that ASCII space U+0020 (a Zs) IS printable. Verified: escaped => Cc (0x00-0x1F, 0x7F-0x9F), Cf (00AD, 061C, 180E, 200B, FEFF), Cs surrogates (DC80-DCFF from surrogateescape), Co private use (E000, F0000), Cn unassigned/noncharacters (0378, FFFE, FDD0, 1FFFE), Zl (2028), Zp (2029), Zs (00A0, 2000, 3000). Raw => all L*, M* (incl. combining U+0301 and astral Mn U+E01EF), N*, P*, S* (incl. emoji U+1F389, U+1D11E, U+FFFD, U+00A1, U+2013), and U+0020.
     In Node, a practical implementation: raw if /\p{L}|\p{M}|\p{N}|\p{P}|\p{S}/u tests true for the char, or the char is " " (U+0020); otherwise escape. (Equivalently: escape if /\p{C}|\p{Z}/u matches and the char isn't U+0020.) Note \p{Cn} is not directly expressible — unassigned code points match none of L/M/N/P/S/Z/C-except-Cn, so the "raw only if L/M/N/P/S or space" formulation handles them correctly (they get escaped).

str() lines (lines 2-4): NO quotes, NO escaping whatsoever. Emit the key's bytes verbatim; a key containing LF/TAB/quotes/control bytes will physically break the "one line per print" appearance. Non-ASCII goes out as raw UTF-8.

ARGV DECODING (affects which code points exist at all): argv bytes are decoded as UTF-8 with the surrogateescape error handler — every undecodable byte 0xNN becomes code point U+DC00+NN (so 0xFF -> U+DCFF -> reprs as \udcff). Encoding back to stdout also uses UTF-8/surrogateescape, so those lone surrogates round-trip to the original raw byte on the str() lines with rc=0 and no exception. In Node: read argv as raw bytes (process.argv is already lossy — if byte-exactness for invalid UTF-8 matters, read /proc/self/cmdline) and implement the same surrogateescape mapping in both directions.

result.implementationNotes:
KEY HANDLING (verbatim, no processing)
1. Take each --kN value exactly as the OS handed it over in argv. No trim, no case folding, no Unicode normalization, no length cap. Empty string is a valid key. Keys are compared by exact code-point sequence: NFC 'é' (C3 A9) != NFD 'e'+U+0301 (65 CC 81) -> two separate entries. 'a' != 'A' != 'a '.
2. NUL is impossible in argv; no handling needed.
3. Invalid UTF-8 in argv must be modeled with Python's surrogateescape: each invalid byte 0xNN maps to code point U+DC00+NN. In Node, read raw argv bytes if you want byte fidelity; when re-emitting a key raw to stdout, map any lone surrogate in U+DC80..U+DCFF back to the single byte (cp - 0xDC00). Node's process.argv already lossy-replaces invalid bytes with U+FFFD, so byte-exact parity requires reading /proc/self/cmdline (split on NUL) rather than process.argv.

REPR OF A KEY (implement Python 3 str.__repr__ exactly)
- Choose the quote char: if the string contains U+0027 (') and does not contain U+0022 ("), use '"'; otherwise use "'".
- Emit quote, then per code point:
  * if cp == chosen quote char -> backslash + that char
  * if cp == 0x5C (backslash) -> two backslashes
  * if cp == 0x0A -> \n ; 0x0D -> \r ; 0x09 -> \t
  * else if the code point is NOT printable (Python str.isprintable(): false for categories Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, Zs — note ASCII space U+0020 IS treated as printable, but U+00A0 and U+2000-family are NOT) -> escape numerically with lowercase hex: cp <= 0xFF -> \xNN (2 digits); cp <= 0xFFFF -> \uNNNN (4 digits); else -> \UNNNNNNNN (8 digits, capital U). Lone surrogates (U+DCFF from surrogateescape) fall here -> \udcff.
  * else emit the character raw as UTF-8 (includes all accented letters, CJK, combining marks like U+0301, and emoji such as U+1F600).
- Emit closing quote. The non-chosen quote char is NEVER escaped.

WHOLE-LINE FORMAT
- Line 1 and line 5: `bidict({` + entries joined by `, ` + `})` where each entry is `<key repr>: <int>`. Exactly one space after each colon, exactly ", " between entries. Ints are plain decimal, negatives as `-5`, no quotes, no separators. Order = key insertion order, and re-assigning an existing key keeps its original position.
- Line 2 = str(b[k1]) -> the integer as decimal.
- Lines 3 and 4 = b.inv[v2] and b.inv[v3] -> the KEY string written RAW: no quotes, no escaping, raw UTF-8 (or raw surrogateescape byte). Consequence: a key containing LF makes that "line" span multiple output lines, so the port must not assume 5 stdout lines; just write key + "
".
- b.inv[v] always yields a plain string (keys are always str), never an int or other type.

STREAM / ENCODING
- stdout is UTF-8 with surrogateescape error handling, unconditionally. No BOM. Not affected by LC_ALL, LANG, PYTHONIOENCODING, or PYTHONUTF8 (all six variants produced byte-identical output). Porter: write UTF-8 buffers to fd 1; ignore locale.
- Terminator is always a single LF (0x0A) after every print, including the last line — the final byte of a successful run is 0x0A. Never CRLF.

ARGPARSE SPECIFICS FOR STRING OPTS
- `--kN VALUE` and `--kN=VALUE` both accepted; `--kN=` gives "". A space-separated value starting with '-' is rejected: stderr `usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3\ntest8_executable: error: argument --kN: expected one argument\n`, rc=2. Use `--kN=-x` to pass a leading-dash key.
- Prefix abbreviation on: `--k` -> `test8_executable: error: ambiguous option: --k could match --k1, --k2, --k3`, rc=2. Unambiguous prefixes like `--k1` are already full names.
- Repeated option: last wins.

ERROR CASES REACHABLE VIA KEY COLLISIONS
- k1==k2 (or any pair equal): later assignment overwrites, entry count shrinks, original position retained, rc=0.
- all three keys equal: bidict holds only the last value; `print(b)` and `print(b[k1])` succeed, then `b.inv[v2]` raises. stderr exactly:
  `Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File "test8.py", line 22, in <module>\n  File "bidict/_base.py", line 524, in __getitem__\nKeyError: 2\n[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!\n`, rc=1. (KeyError arg is repr of the int.) Note if v2 happens to equal the surviving value, no error and the run completes.
- final `b[k1] = 999` when 999 is held by a DIFFERENT key: rc=1, stderr traceback frames `test8.py line 26 in <module>` / `bidict/_bidict.py line 80 in __setitem__` / `bidict/_bidict.py line 106 in put` / `bidict/_base.py line 454 in _update` / `bidict/_base.py line 333 in _dedup`, final message `bidict.KeyAndValueDuplicationError: ('a', 999)` — tuple is (k1, 999). If k1 already holds 999, it is a silent no-op and the two repr lines are identical.
- The `[PYI-<n>:ERROR]` number is the PID and is nondeterministic.

result.implementationNotes:
STREAMS/EXIT: all normal output on stdout, each line \n-terminated. Every uncaught-exception path writes the whole traceback to stderr and exits rc=1. stdout produced before the exception IS flushed and kept.

NO CARET LINES: because this is a frozen build without embedded source, tracebacks contain NO source-echo lines and NO '^^^' / '~^^^' caret lines at all. cat -A confirmed. Do not emit them.

=== THE ONLY TWO TRACEBACK SHAPES ===

(A) __setitem__ duplication error (6 lines + trailer), byte exact:
"Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
"  File \"test8.py\", line <L>, in <module>\n"
"  File \"bidict/_bidict.py\", line 80, in __setitem__\n"
"  File \"bidict/_bidict.py\", line 106, in put\n"
"  File \"bidict/_base.py\", line 454, in _update\n"
"  File \"bidict/_base.py\", line <D>, in _dedup\n"
"bidict.<Class>: <payload>\n"
"[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!\n"
where <D> = 347 and <Class> = ValueDuplicationError, payload = decimalString(value);
   or <D> = 333 and <Class> = KeyAndValueDuplicationError, payload = "(" + pyRepr(key) + ", " + decimalString(value) + ")".
<L> = 16 for the b[k2]=v2 write, 17 for the b[k3]=v3 write, 26 for the final b[k1]=999 write. (Write 1, b[k1]=v1, can never fail: the bidict is empty.)

(B) b.inv[...] KeyError (4 lines + trailer), byte exact:
"Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
"  File \"test8.py\", line 22, in <module>\n"
"  File \"bidict/_base.py\", line 524, in __getitem__\n"
"KeyError: " + decimalString(value) + "\n"
"[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!\n"
Line 22 is print(b.inv[v2]). No other KeyError line number is ever observable (see reachability below).

=== DECISION TABLE for b[k] = v ===
Let K = (k is an existing key), V = (v is currently bound to some key k_owner).
1. !K and !V            -> INSERT: append k at the end of the key order; bind k<->v.
2.  K and !V            -> OVERWRITE: unbind (k, oldValue) — delete oldValue from the inverse COMPLETELY — then bind k<->v. Key k KEEPS its original insertion position (never moves to the end).
3. !K and  V            -> raise ValueDuplicationError(v). Nothing is mutated.
4.  K and  V and k_owner == k  (i.e. b[k] is already v) -> NO-OP, silent, position and content unchanged.
5.  K and  V and k_owner != k  -> raise KeyAndValueDuplicationError((k, v)). Nothing is mutated.
KeyDuplicationError is UNREACHABLE from __setitem__: bidict's default OnDup for __setitem__ is (key=DROP_OLD, val=RAISE), so a key duplicate is silently resolved by overwrite (case 2/4) and never raised. KeyDuplicationError only comes from put()/putall() with on_dup_key=RAISE, which this program never calls. A porter can omit it entirely.
Because __setitem__ never removes a KEY (case 3 and 5 abort without mutating), a key inserted at write 1 is present forever. Therefore at write 4 (b[k1]=999) k1 is ALWAYS present, so write 4 can only take case 4 (no-op, when b[k1]==999) or case 5 (KeyAndValueDuplicationError). Write 4 can NEVER raise ValueDuplicationError — verified by construction and by the '--v1 999 --k2 a' / '--v3 999' probes.

=== ORDERING RULE ===
Maintain an insertion-ordered map keyed by key (JS Map already does this). Case 2 must update the value in place (Map.set on an existing key preserves position) — do NOT delete-then-set. Confirmed: k1==k2 gives "bidict({'a': 2, 'c': 3})" (a first), k1==k3 gives "bidict({'a': 3, 'b': 2})" (a first, b second), and after b[k1]=999 the key order is still unchanged.

=== INVERSE UNBIND PROOF ===
Case 2 must delete the old value from the inverse index. Proven two ways: (a) "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 a --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 1" succeeds -> value 1 was free for a new key; (b) "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 b --v3 3" then reading b.inv[2] raises KeyError: 2.

=== REACHABILITY OF THE THREE READS ===
print(b[k1])   -> can NEVER KeyError (k1 always present).
print(b.inv[v2]) -> KeyErrors exactly when k2 == k3 AND v2 != v3 (includes k1==k2==k3 shapes). All other reachable states keep v2 bound.
print(b.inv[v3]) -> can NEVER KeyError: v3 is bound by the immediately preceding successful write and nothing between removes it. (Any conflict that would remove it aborts earlier with a duplication error.)

=== VALUE FORMATTING ===
Values are Python ints of unbounded precision (parse with BigInt). Rendered everywhere (repr, plain print, error payloads, KeyError) as bare decimal, no quotes, no thousands separators, leading '-' for negatives, and '-0' normalizes to '0'. Equality/lookup is numeric, so '-0' collides with '0' and '007' would collide with '7'.

=== KEY FORMATTING (Python str repr) ===
Prefer single quotes; if the string contains a "'" and no '"', use double quotes instead and leave the "'" unescaped; if it contains both, use single quotes and escape "'" as "\\'". Escape backslash as \\\\, newline as \\n, tab as \\t, CR as \\r. Leave all other printable characters, including non-ASCII (é, →, emoji), as raw UTF-8 — no \\u escaping. Empty string -> ''. This same repr is used both in the bidict(...) repr and inside the KeyAndValueDuplicationError tuple. Note the plain `print(b.inv[...])` lines print the key RAW (no quotes, no escaping).

=== REPR ===
"bidict({" + entries.map(([k,v]) => pyRepr(k) + ": " + dec(v)).join(", ") + "})"; empty map would be "bidict({})" (not reachable here since write 1 always succeeds).

result.implementationNotes:
JS reimplementation of Python int(s) for argparse type=int. Return a BigInt (never a Number: 9007199254740993 and 26+-digit values must round-trip exactly; printing uses BigInt.toString()).

STEP 0 - argparse pre-filter (happens BEFORE int() is called). For a space-separated token following --vN: if the token starts with '-' and does NOT match /^-\d+$/ and does NOT match /^-\d*\.\d+$/, argparse treats it as an option string, so you must emit:
  line1: "usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3"
  line2: "test8_executable: error: argument --v1: expected one argument"
on stderr, rc=2 (e.g. "-1_000", "-x", "--5"). The "--vN=VALUE" form skips this check entirely, so "--v1=-1_000" reaches int() and yields -1000. Digits here are ASCII-only \d.

STEP 1 - decode argv. Iterate over Unicode CODE POINTS (use [...s] / codePointAt, not UTF-16 units) so astral digits like U+104A5 work. Undecodable argv bytes must already have been mapped to U+DC80+byte (surrogateescape) by the argv reader.

STEP 2 - transform (mirrors CPython PyUnicode_TransformDecimalAndSpaceToASCII). For each code point cp:
  - if cp < 0x80: keep as-is.
  - else if cp is Unicode-whitespace (see set W below): replace with ASCII ' ' (0x20).
  - else if cp has a Unicode DECIMAL digit value (general category Nd only): replace with the ASCII digit '0'+value.
  - else: keep as-is (it will make the parse fail).
  Set W (Py_UNICODE_ISSPACE for cp >= 0x80), verified accepted: U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000..U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000. Verified NOT whitespace: U+180E, U+200B, U+2060, U+FEFF.
  Nd detection: use /\p{Nd}/u plus a value table, or compute value = cp - blockStart for the matched Nd block. Verified accepted digit blocks include Arabic-Indic U+0660.., Devanagari U+0966.., Bengali U+09E6.., Thai U+0E50.., Fullwidth U+FF10.., Osmanya U+104A0... Verified rejected: U+00B2 (No), U+00BD (No), U+2164 (Nl), U+2465 (No).

STEP 3 - ASCII parse of the transformed string t:
  1. Strip leading and trailing characters in exactly {0x09 \t, 0x0A \n, 0x0B \v, 0x0C \f, 0x0D \r, 0x20 space}. NOTE: 0x1C..0x1F must NOT be stripped even though Python's str.isspace() calls them whitespace — int() rejects them.
  2. Optional single sign: one '+' or one '-'. Two signs, or a sign alone, is invalid.
  3. The remainder must match /^[0-9](?:_?[0-9])*$/ : at least one digit, underscores only BETWEEN digits, never doubled, never leading (also not directly after the sign), never trailing. Leading zeros are fine.
  4. Remove underscores, BigInt(digits), negate if '-'. '-0' yields 0n (prints "0").
  5. Anything else (empty, whitespace-only, base prefixes 0x/0b/0o, decimal points, exponents, 'inf', 'nan', internal whitespace, non-Nd numerics, stray chars) -> ValueError.

STEP 4 - error output on failure. rc=2, stdout empty, stderr = usage line + "\n" + "test8_executable: error: argument " + optName + ": invalid int value: " + pyRepr(ORIGINAL untransformed string) + "\n". optName is the first offending option in command-line order (--v1, then --v2, then --v3); parsing aborts at the first failure.

pyRepr(s) (Python str.__repr__), needed byte-exactly:
  a) Choose the wrapper quote: default "'". If s contains "'" and does NOT contain '"', use '"' instead. (If it contains both, wrapper stays "'".)
  b) For each code point: backslash -> "\\\\" (two chars); the wrapper quote char -> backslash + that char; 0x0A -> "\\n"; 0x0D -> "\\r"; 0x09 -> "\\t"; other NON-PRINTABLE code points -> "\\xHH" (cp < 0x100), "\\uHHHH" (cp < 0x10000), "\\UHHHHHHHH" (cp >= 0x10000), all lowercase hex, zero-padded to 2/4/8; everything else emitted verbatim as UTF-8.
  c) "Non-printable" = Python str.isprintable() is False = Unicode general categories Cc, Cf, Cs, Co, Cn, Zl, Zp, Zs — EXCEPT that U+0020 space itself IS printable and emitted raw. Confirmed instances: 0x01->'\\x01', 0x0b->'\\x0b', 0x7f->'\\x7f', U+00AD->'\\xad', U+00A0->'\\xa0', U+200B->'\\u200b', U+2060->'\\u2060', U+FEFF->'\\ufeff', U+180E->'\\u180e', U+1D173->'\\U0001d173', surrogate U+DCFF->'\\udcff'. Printable and therefore raw: 'é', '中', '😀', combining U+0301, U+00B2, U+2164, U+2465, U+00BD.
  d) Wrap with the chosen quote on both sides.

Non-int notes worth carrying: the final `b[k1] = 999` step compares against 999n — if any of v1/v2/v3 was supplied as 999 for a key other than k1 the program dies with rc=1 after printing the first 4 stdout lines and a traceback ending "bidict.KeyAndValueDuplicationError: ('<k1>', 999)" plus a "[PYI-NNNN:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!" line whose numeric code varies run to run. If v1 == 999 the update is a silent no-op.

result.implementationNotes:
PROG NAME
- prog = basename(argv[0]) with extension kept (verified via copy, symlink, ./relative, and a name with a space). In Node: `const prog = path.basename(process.argv[1])`. Used in three places: the usage line, the `${prog}: error: ` prefix, and --help.

CANONICAL STRINGS (default width, i.e. COLUMNS unset/empty/non-numeric/>=78)
- USAGE (one line, no trailing space):
  `usage: ${prog} [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3`
- HELP (stdout, rc 0), exactly 193 bytes for prog=test8_executable:
  USAGE + "\n" + "\n" + "options:\n" + "  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n" + "  --k1 K1\n" + "  --v1 V1\n" + "  --k2 K2\n" + "  --v2 V2\n" + "  --k3 K3\n" + "  --v3 V3\n"
  (2-space indent for every option row; the `-h, --help` row has exactly 2 spaces between `--help` and `show`; the `--kN KN` / `--vN VN` rows have NO help text and NO trailing whitespace.)
- ERROR OUTPUT (stderr, rc 2) is always: USAGE + "\n" + `${prog}: error: ${msg}` + "\n". The msg line is never wrapped.

OPTION TABLE (declaration order matters for every list-producing message)
  ['--k1','--v1','--k2','--v2','--k3','--v3'], plus '-h'/'--help'. --kN are strings, --vN go through int().

PARSING ALGORITHM (order of operations — this ordering is load-bearing)
1. PRE-SCAN: classify each argv token left-to-right. For a token starting with '--':
   a. split at the first '=' into (name, explicitArg?) but first check the FULL token against exact option strings.
   b. exact match on the full token -> that option, no explicit arg.
   c. exact match on `name` (part before '=') -> that option with explicitArg.
   d. otherwise collect all defined option strings that START WITH the token (or with `name`). If >1 distinct options match -> IMMEDIATELY error, rc 2:
      `ambiguous option: ${originalToken} could match ${matches.join(', ')}`  (originalToken includes any '=value'; matches in declaration order, e.g. `--k1, --k2, --k3`).
      If exactly 1 -> resolve to it. If 0 -> mark UNKNOWN (do NOT error yet).
   This pre-scan ambiguity error fires before ANY int conversion or required check. Proof: `--v1 x --k` reports the ambiguity, not the bad int.
2. Walk tokens. On '-h'/'--help' (or any unambiguous prefix of --help: --h, --he, --hel; also `-hh` which is short-clustered as -h -h): print HELP to stdout, exit 0 immediately. Help wins over everything (missing required, unknown args, junk).
   - But if help got an explicit arg (`--help=x`, `-h=x`): error rc 2 with `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'` (note: BOTH option strings joined by '/'; the value is single-quoted).
3. For a resolved --kN/--vN with an explicitArg (from '='): use it verbatim, even if it looks like an option (`--k1=-x` -> '-x') and even if empty (`--k1=` -> '').
4. For a resolved --kN/--vN without explicitArg: consume the next token as the value, but ONLY if it does not "look like an option". A token looks like an option if it starts with '-' AND is longer than 1 char AND is not a negative number (regex ^-\d+$ or ^-\d*\.\d+$). So: '-x' and '--' and '--v1' look like options; '-', '-5', '-3.2' do NOT. If no usable value: error rc 2 with `argument ${optionString}: expected one argument` (single option string, e.g. `--k1`, `--v3`).
5. For --vN, convert with Python-int semantics right at consumption time. On failure: error rc 2 with `argument ${optionString}: invalid int value: '${raw}'` (raw single-quoted). Only the FIRST failing occurrence in argv order is reported.
6. Repeated options: LAST occurrence wins (plain store).
7. A bare '--' token: argparse consumes the first '--' as a positional-pattern separator, so everything after it is a positional/leftover; but in the concrete observed cases the '--' itself STILL shows up in the unrecognized list when required args were all satisfied (`<all args> --` -> `unrecognized arguments: --`; `<all args> -- foo` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- foo`). And '--' immediately after an option does NOT escape the next token: `--k1 -- a ...` -> `argument --k1: expected one argument`.
8. AFTER the walk, check required. If any of the 6 are absent -> error rc 2:
   `the following arguments are required: ${missing.join(', ')}` where `missing` is in DECLARATION order (--k1,--v1,--k2,--v2,--k3,--v3) regardless of user supply order; separator is exactly comma+space; a single missing item has no comma.
9. Only if required all satisfied, report leftovers -> error rc 2:
   `unrecognized arguments: ${extras.join(' ')}` — leftovers in ARGV order, joined by a single SPACE. An unknown long/short option also swallows its following value into extras (`--bogus x` -> two extras `--bogus`,`x` printed as `--bogus x`). An empty-string leftover yields a trailing space: `unrecognized arguments: ` + "\n".

ERROR PRECEDENCE (highest first), all rc 2 except help (rc 0):
  ambiguous option (pre-scan) > help action (or its 'ignored explicit argument') > expected one argument / invalid int value (argv order, first hit) > the following arguments are required > unrecognized arguments.
  Corollaries verified: `--k1 a extra` -> required error (extras never mentioned); `--bogus x` alone -> required error; `--k1 a --v1 x ... --bogus` -> invalid int error.

CASE / ALIAS RULES
- Matching is case-sensitive: `--K1` is unknown.
- Single-dash `-k1` is NOT an alias for `--k1`; it becomes an unknown token and its following value becomes a leftover.
- `--k1x` is not an abbreviation (must be a prefix, not a superstring) -> unknown.

WIDTH SENSITIVITY (optional fidelity)
- Text budget = COLUMNS - 2, default 80 (so 78). COLUMNS empty or non-numeric -> 80.
- Only the usage block wraps; the `prog: error: ...` line never wraps.
- Wrapped usage continuation indent = len('usage: ') + len(prog) + 1 spaces (24 for test8_executable) while the prog still fits on line 1; at very narrow widths the layout switches to prog alone on line 1 with all optionals wrapped at a 7-space indent.
- Option help column also narrows (14 -> 8 -> 4 spaces) as COLUMNS shrinks. Most ports can just hardcode the default-width strings.

RUNTIME (non-argparse) ERROR SHAPE, for reference
- Frozen tracebacks have NO source lines under each `File` entry and end with:
  `[PYI-2028:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!` on stderr, rc 1.
- Observed ValueDuplicationError stack: `File "test8.py", line 16, in <module>` / `File "bidict/_bidict.py", line 80, in __setitem__` / `File "bidict/_bidict.py", line 106, in put` / `File "bidict/_base.py", line 454, in _update` / `File "bidict/_base.py", line 347, in _dedup` / `bidict.ValueDuplicationError: 2`.

result.implementationNotes:
GOAL: reproduce stderr byte-exactly for the 3 reachable exception classes. rc is 1 for all of them (argparse errors are rc=2 and are a different dimension).

--- WHICH ERROR IS REACHABLE WHERE ---
Simulate the script literally, in order. Let `b` be an insertion-ordered map key->int and `inv` the reverse map.
- line 15 `b[k1]=v1`: can NEVER raise (empty bidict).
- line 16 `b[k2]=v2`: raises ValueDuplicationError(v2) iff (k2 != k1) and (v2 == v1). If k2 == k1: overwrite (or no-op if v2==v1), never raises. KeyAndValueDuplicationError is impossible here (only one item exists).
- line 17 `b[k3]=v3`: two distinct outcomes -
    * if k3 is NOT a current key and v3 is already a value -> ValueDuplicationError(v3)   [_dedup line 347]
    * if k3 IS a current key and v3 is held by a DIFFERENT key -> KeyAndValueDuplicationError(k3, v3)   [_dedup line 333]
    * if k3 IS a current key and v3 is its own current value -> silent no-op
- line 18 `print(b)`, line 21 `print(b[k1])`: never raise (k1 is always present).
- line 22 `print(b.inv[v2])`: raises bare KeyError(v2) iff v2 is not a current value. Only reachable when k3 == k2 and v3 != v2.
- line 23 `print(b.inv[v3])`: UNREACHABLE failure. v3 is always a current value. Do not implement.
- line 26 `b[k1]=999`: raises KeyAndValueDuplicationError(k1, 999) iff 999 is held by some key != k1. If b[k1]==999 already -> no-op, rc=0.
Note bidict's __setitem__ uses on_dup key=DROP_OLD, so KeyDuplicationError is NEVER reachable.

--- EXACT STDERR TEMPLATES ---
Let SRCBLOCK(L) be the two extra lines described below (may be omitted, see SOURCE ECHO).

(A) ValueDuplicationError, L in {16,17}:
"Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
"  File \"test8.py\", line {L}, in <module>\n"
[SRCBLOCK(L)]
"  File \"bidict/_bidict.py\", line 80, in __setitem__\n"
"  File \"bidict/_bidict.py\", line 106, in put\n"
"  File \"bidict/_base.py\", line 454, in _update\n"
"  File \"bidict/_base.py\", line 347, in _dedup\n"
"bidict.ValueDuplicationError: {intstr(v)}\n"
"[PYI-{pid}:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!\n"

(B) KeyAndValueDuplicationError, L in {17,26}: identical to (A) except the last internal frame is
"  File \"bidict/_base.py\", line 333, in _dedup\n"
and the message line is
"bidict.KeyAndValueDuplicationError: ({pyrepr(key)}, {intstr(v)})\n"
(333 vs 347 is the ONLY frame-line difference between the two duplication errors. Frames 80/106/454 are identical.)

(C) KeyError, L == 22 only:
"Traceback (most recent call last):\n"
"  File \"test8.py\", line 22, in <module>\n"
[SRCBLOCK(22)]
"  File \"bidict/_base.py\", line 524, in __getitem__\n"
"KeyError: {intstr(v2)}\n"
"[PYI-{pid}:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!\n"
(Only ONE internal frame; no "bidict." prefix on KeyError.)

--- SOURCE ECHO (SRCBLOCK) ---
Two lines, each ending \n. Leading spaces verified with od -c:
  L=16: "    b[args.k2] = args.v2\n"  +  "    ~^^^^^^^^^\n"      (4 spaces, then 1 '~' then 9 '^')
  L=17: "    b[args.k3] = args.v3\n"  +  "    ~^^^^^^^^^\n"
  L=26: "    b[args.k1] = 999\n"      +  "    ~^^^^^^^^^\n"
  L=22: "    print(b.inv[args.v2])\n" +  "          ~~~~~^^^^^^^^^\n"   (10 spaces, then 5 '~' then 9 '^')
SRCBLOCK is present ONLY if a readable file named "test8.py" resolves from the process CWD (Python linecache). /workspace/dataset ships test8.py, so running with cwd=/workspace/dataset yields the WITH-source form; running from any other directory yields the bare 1-line frame. Recommend emitting the WITH-source form (hardcoded strings above) since the reference binary is normally exercised from its own directory. Internal bidict frames never carry source lines.
Total stderr byte counts for cross-checking: VDE 414 with / 375 without; KVDE@17 427/388; KVDE@26 429/390; KeyError@22 313/216.

--- pyrepr(key) (Python str repr) ---
quote = "'"; if key contains "'" and not '"': quote = '"'.
Escape inside: backslash -> "\\\\", \n -> "\\n", \r -> "\\r", \t -> "\\t", the chosen quote char -> "\\" + quote, other chars with codepoint < 0x20 or == 0x7f -> "\\x%02x". Printable non-ASCII (é, 中, ...) emitted RAW as UTF-8 - never \\u escaped. Empty string -> "''".
intstr(v) = plain decimal, "-" prefix for negatives, arbitrary precision (use BigInt if you parse big ints).

--- PYI-NNN ---
NNN is the PID of the frozen child process; it is NOT input-derived and NOT stable across runs (verified: 5 identical runs gave 746/756/785/776/766; backgrounding showed PYI == $! + 1). Emit `process.pid`. Tell the grader this field is inherently non-reproducible; the rest of stderr is fully deterministic.

--- STREAM ORDER / FLUSHING ---
stdout produced before the exception is always emitted in full (KVDE@26 -> 4 lines; KeyError@22 -> 2 lines; VDE@16/17 and KVDE@17 -> 0 lines). When stdout is NOT a tty, Python block-buffers it and flushes at exit, so in a merged (2>&1) pipe the whole traceback + PYI line come FIRST, then the stdout lines. On a tty, stdout is line-buffered and appears BEFORE the traceback. To match, a Node port should buffer stdout and flush it after writing stderr when !process.stdout.isTTY. No BrokenPipeError is reachable (`| head -1` gives rc=0, empty stderr).

--- OTHER ---
Nothing else ever appears on stderr: successful runs produce exactly 0 bytes of stderr, no warnings. PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii does not trigger UnicodeEncodeError; non-ASCII keys round-trip as raw UTF-8 on both streams.
Relevant files: /workspace/dataset/test8_executable, /workspace/dataset/test8.py (line numbers 15,16,17,18,21,22,23,26 match the traceback because the file has two Chinese comments at lines 13 and 20 plus a blank line 19).

gaps.gap: Mid-argv bare `--` terminates ALL option parsing — no probe tested `--` anywhere except position 0 and trailing. Everything after the first `--` becomes an extra/positional, so options after it are NOT parsed and are reported as MISSING. Observed: `--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b -- --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3` -> rc=2, `test8_executable: error: the following arguments are required: --v2, --k3, --v3`. And `--k1 a -- --v1 x --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3` -> `the following arguments are required: --v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3` (the bad int `x` is never converted). This is the single largest missing rule; a port implementing the spec's left-to-right walk without a `--` terminator will diverge on any input containing `--`.
gaps.why: The spec only documented `--` at the very start or very end, and hand-waved it as 'argparse consumes the first -- as a positional-pattern separator'. The real rule is a hard parse terminator at any index.
gaps.command: cd /workspace/dataset && for a in "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b -- --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3" "--k1 a -- --v1 x --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3" "--k1 a --v1 1 -- --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3"; do echo "=== $a"; ./test8_executable $a >/tmp/o.txt 2>/tmp/e.txt; echo RC=$?; cat -A /tmp/o.txt; cat -A /tmp/e.txt; done

gaps.gap: The ambiguous-option 'pre-scan' STOPS at the first `--`. Observed: `-- --k` -> rc=2 `the following arguments are required: --k1, --v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3` (NOT `ambiguous option: --k`), and `<all 6 args> -- --k` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- --k` (NOT ambiguous). So the pre-classification pass must break on `--` and mark every remaining token as a positional.
gaps.why: The spec says the pre-scan classifies 'each argv token left-to-right' and 'IMMEDIATELY errors' on ambiguity, with no `--` exception. A port following that would emit an ambiguity error where the real binary emits a required/unrecognized error.
gaps.command: cd /workspace/dataset && for a in "-- --k" "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3 -- --k" "--k --help" "--help --k"; do echo "=== $a"; ./test8_executable $a 2>&1 | tail -1 | cat -A; done

gaps.gap: `--` is NEVER stripped from the extras list. `<all 6 args> -- --` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- --` (both survive); `<all 6> -- -- foo` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- -- foo`; `<all 6> -- -h` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- -h` (help does NOT fire). The spec's claim that 'argparse only strips the FIRST -- it consumes' is false for this parser (it defines no positionals, so `_get_values` never runs and nothing is stripped).
gaps.why: A port that drops the first `--` from the leftover list produces the wrong `unrecognized arguments:` string.
gaps.command: cd /workspace/dataset && for a in "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3 --" "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3 -- --" "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3 -- -- foo" "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3 -- -h"; do echo "=== $a"; ./test8_executable $a 2>&1 | tail -1 | cat -A; done

gaps.gap: Short-option clustering rule for `-h` is stated wrong. The real rule: any single-dash token whose FIRST character after '-' is 'h' fires help and ignores the rest — `-hh`, `-hx`, `-h5` all print help, rc=0. But `-xh` does NOT (unknown token `-xh`, reported verbatim as one extra / triggers the required error). And `-h=x` / `-h=` / `--help=` / `--hel=x` all give `argument -h/--help: ignored explicit argument 'x'` / `... ''` — note the EMPTY explicit arg form `''` was never captured by any probe.
gaps.why: The spec explains `-hh` as '-h then -h', which wrongly predicts `-xh` -> help and gives no rule for `-hx`/`-h5`. The `''` payload for `-h=` / `--help=` is a distinct message a port must emit.
gaps.command: cd /workspace/dataset && for a in "-hh" "-hx" "-h5" "-xh" "-h=x" "-h=" "--help=" "--hel=x"; do echo "=== $a"; ./test8_executable $a >/tmp/o.txt 2>/tmp/e.txt; echo RC=$?; head -1 /tmp/o.txt|cat -A; tail -1 /tmp/e.txt|cat -A; done

gaps.gap: COLUMNS<=0 falls back to width 80, not to a tiny width. Observed: `COLUMNS=0` and `COLUMNS=-5` both produce the full unwrapped 76-char usage line, while `COLUMNS=1`/`2`/`5`/`7`..`11` all produce the identical maximally-wrapped layout (prog on line 1, then each token on its own 7-space-indented line). So the rule is: parse COLUMNS as int; if it fails OR the value is <= 0, use 80; and the wrap layout saturates at width<=~11.
gaps.why: The spec only said 'COLUMNS empty or non-numeric -> 80'. A port doing `width = Number(COLUMNS) || 80` accidentally gets 0 right but `-5` wrong.
gaps.command: cd /workspace/dataset && for c in 0 -5 1 2 5 7 8 9 10 11 12 200; do echo "=== COLUMNS=$c"; COLUMNS=$c ./test8_executable 2>&1 | cat -A; done

gaps.gap: When stdout IS a tty and COLUMNS is unset, argparse uses the ACTUAL terminal width, not 80. Observed under `script` with `stty cols 40`: the usage block wraps at 24-space continuation indent exactly like `COLUMNS=40`. No probe tested this; all six probes ran with pipes/files.
gaps.why: If the grading harness ever runs the reference or the port on a pty, a port that hardcodes 80 diverges. Node equivalent: `process.stdout.columns`.
gaps.command: cd /workspace/dataset && env -u COLUMNS script -qec "stty cols 40; /workspace/dataset/test8_executable" /dev/null 2>&1 | cat -A

gaps.gap: An unknown option swallows a RUN of following non-option tokens, not just one value, and stops at the next KNOWN option. Observed: `<all 6> --bogus x y --k1 z` -> `unrecognized arguments: --bogus x y` (the trailing `--k1 z` is parsed normally); `--bogus --k1 a --v1 1 ...` -> `unrecognized arguments: --bogus` only (all six parse fine, rc=2 solely because of the extra).

gaps.command: cd /workspace/dataset && for a in "--bogus --k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3" "--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3 --bogus x y --k1 z" "-x a --k1 A --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 --k3 c --v3 3"; do echo "=== $a"; ./test8_executable $a 2>&1 | tail -1 | cat -A; done

result.implementationNotes:
GAP CONFIRMED: `--` is NEVER stripped. The spec claim "argparse only strips the FIRST -- it consumes" is FALSE for this parser. Reason: the parser declares zero positionals, so argparse's `_get_values` (the only place that removes a leading `--` from a positional value list) never runs. Every `--` token flows through to `parse_known_args`'s extras and is printed verbatim.

PORT ALGORITHM (single left-to-right scan over argv[1:]):

State: `terminated = false`, `extras = []` (ordered), `values = {k1:undef, v1:undef, k2:undef, v2:undef, k3:undef, v3:undef}`.
Define PROG = "test8_executable".
Define USAGE = "usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3\n".
Define ERR(msg): write USAGE + PROG + ": error: " + msg + "\n" to STDERR, exit(2).

For each token t at index i:
1. If `terminated` is true: push t to `extras`; continue. (No option parsing, no `-h`, no value consumption, ever again.)
2. If t === "--" (exact 2-char string, not "--x", not "--="): set `terminated = true`, AND push "--" itself to `extras`. Continue. => The terminator token is both consumed as a terminator and retained as an extra. Do this for the FIRST `--` and for every subsequent `--` (subsequent ones just fall through rule 1 to the same push).
3. If t is "-h" or "--help" (or an unambiguous abbreviation of --help): print the help text to STDOUT and exit(0) IMMEDIATELY — before any required-arg or extras check.
4. If t is a known option (--k1/--v1/--k2/--v2/--k3/--v3, incl. `=`-attached form and unambiguous abbreviations): parse it. For the space-separated form, the next token is taken as the value ONLY if it is not "--" and not option-looking; if the next token is "--" or missing, ERR("argument " + optName + ": expected one argument"). NOTE: the `=`-attached form bypasses this entirely — `--k1=--` legitimately assigns the literal string "--".
5. Otherwise (unknown option or bare word): push t to `extras`.

ERROR PRECEDENCE (strict, verified):
  A. Inline scan errors fire first, at the moment they are hit: `-h` help exit (rc=0); `argument <opt>: expected one argument`; `argument <opt>: invalid int value: '<tok>'`.
  B. Then the missing-required check: if any of the six is still unset, ERR("the following arguments are required: " + missing.join(", ")) where `missing` is in PARSER DEFINITION ORDER --k1, --v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3 (NOT argv order). rc=2.
  C. Only if all six are set: if `extras.length > 0`, ERR("unrecognized arguments: " + extras.join(" ")). rc=2.
  D. Only if extras is empty: run the bidict program logic.
Consequence: a `--` early in argv that hides required options yields the REQUIRED error, never the unrecognized error (see `-- --k1 a ...` and `--k1 a --v1 1 -- --k2 b ...`).

MESSAGE FORMATTING DETAILS:
- extras are joined with exactly one ASCII space; no quoting, no shell-escaping. Empty-string tokens contribute zero characters, so they yield double/leading/trailing spaces in the message (e.g. "unrecognized arguments:  -- " with two spaces after the colon and one trailing space before "\n").
- Because of the naive space join, a single argv token "--k1 a" is indistinguishable in output from two tokens "--k1" "a" (both render as `-- --k1 a` in the `-- '--k1 a'` test).
- `=`-form unknown options stay as one token (`--bogus=1`), never split on `=`.
- Unknown long options do NOT swallow a following value; the following token becomes its own separate extra.
- `-` (single dash) is an ordinary extra, never a terminator.
- All error output goes to STDERR with STDOUT completely empty; help output goes to STDOUT with STDERR completely empty (rc=0). Every message ends with exactly one "\n"; no trailing blank line.

HELP TEXT (STDOUT, rc=0, exact):
"usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3\n\noptions:\n  -h, --help  show this help message and exit\n  --k1 K1\n  --v1 V1\n  --k2 K2\n  --v2 V2\n  --k3 K3\n  --v3 V3\n"
(Note "options:" — Python 3.10+ heading, not "optional arguments:". Two-space indent on each entry; "-h, --help" followed by two spaces then the description.)

An isolated rerun with `od -c` proved stderr for that case is exactly 129 bytes = the two lines quoted above. Always use fresh temp files.

result.implementationNotes:
ALGORITHM (replaces any naive left-to-right walk):

Step 0 — locate terminator. `term = argv.indexOf('--')` where the comparison is exact equality to the 2-byte string `--`. Note: `-` and `---` are NOT terminators; `--k1=--` is not a terminator token (the `--` is part of a single argv element after the `=`).

Step 1 — split. `head = argv.slice(0, term)` (or all of argv if term === -1); `tail = term === -1 ? [] : argv.slice(term)` — NOTE `tail` INCLUDES the `--` element itself.

Step 2 — parse only `head`, left-to-right, exactly as the existing spec describes (support `--opt VALUE` and `--opt=VALUE`; `-h`/`--help`). Collect unmatched non-option tokens from `head` into `extrasHead` in order.

Step 3 — `extras = extrasHead.concat(tail)`. Because the parser declares no positional arguments, nothing ever consumes the `--`, so if a bare `--` was present, `extras` is always non-empty.

Step 4 — error/exit precedence, in this exact order (first match wins, later checks never run):
  A. Help: if `-h` or `--help` appears in `head` (at the point it is reached during the left-to-right walk, before any missing/extra check), print the help block to STDOUT and exit 0. Help in `tail` is ignored.
  B. Value-starvation: if an option in `head` is the last token of `head` (i.e. its value slot would be the `--` or end of argv), emit
     `usage: ...\ntest8_executable: error: argument <OPT>: expected one argument\n` to stderr, exit 2. This is detected during the scan, so it beats C and D.
  C. Type error: `argument --vN: invalid int value: '<raw>'` — only reachable for options inside `head`.
  D. Missing required: if any of `--k1 --v1 --k2 --v2 --k3 --v3` was not seen in `head`, emit
     `usage: ...\ntest8_executable: error: the following arguments are required: ` + missing.join(', ') + `\n`
     where `missing` is filtered in DECLARATION order `[--k1, --v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3]` regardless of argv order. Exit 2. Extras are NOT mentioned.
  E. Unrecognized extras: if `extras.length > 0`, emit
     `usage: ...\ntest8_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: ` + extras.join(' ') + `\n`
     Exit 2. No quoting/escaping of any kind: empty-string elements produce empty fields (so a single trailing space before the LF), and elements containing spaces are printed raw.
  F. Only now run the bidict body. Consequence: argparse errors ALWAYS pre-empt bidict.ValueDuplicationError / KeyAndValueDuplicationError.

COROLLARY the porter must not miss: since no positionals are declared, ANY argv containing a bare `--` token exits with rc=2 and empty stdout — either via D or via E. There is no `--`-containing invocation that prints the 5 bidict lines. The only way a literal `--` reaches the data is `--k1=--` (or `--k2=--`/`--k3=--`), which succeeds and renders as the key `'--'` inside the repr.

The usage line is the constant first stderr line in every error case:
`usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3`

Full help text (stdout, rc=0), byte-exact:
```
usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --k1 K1
  --v1 V1
  --k2 K2
  --v2 V2
  --k3 K3
  --v3 V3
```
(blank line after usage; `options:` lowercase with colon; two-space indent; `-h, --help` followed by two spaces then the description.)

result.implementationNotes:
TERMINATOR-AWARE PRE-CLASSIFICATION (replaces the spec's \"classify each argv token left-to-right, immediately error on ambiguity\"):

Pass 1 — build a class array over argv, one entry per token, in order. Maintain `sawTerminator = false`.
  for i, tok of argv:
    if !sawTerminator && tok === "--"  (EXACT byte equality; not "-", not "", not "---k", not "--k1=--"):
        class[i] = "DASHDASH"; sawTerminator = true; continue    // do NOT run option classification on this token
    if sawTerminator:
        class[i] = "POSITIONAL"; continue                        // unconditionally, for EVERY remaining token
    // normal classification, which is the ONLY place ambiguity can be raised:
    class[i] = classifyOption(tok)   // "OPTION" or "POSITIONAL"

  classifyOption(tok) rules that matter here:
    - "" (empty), "-" -> POSITIONAL, no ambiguity check.
    - exact match in the option table ("--k1", "-h", ...) -> OPTION.
    - starts with "--" and contains "=": split at FIRST "=" into head/value; prefix-match head.
    - otherwise prefix-match the whole token against long option strings.
    - if exactly one long option starts with the head -> OPTION (abbreviation accepted).
    - if 2+ match -> IMMEDIATELY exit(2): print usage line to stderr, then
      `test8_executable: error: ambiguous option: <FULL ORIGINAL TOKEN> could match <matches joined by ", ">`
      NOTE: <FULL ORIGINAL TOKEN> includes any "=value" suffix (e.g. `ambiguous option: --k=x could match --k1, --k2, --k3`).
      Matches are listed in declaration order: --k1, --v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3 (so `--k` -> `--k1, --k2, --k3`; `--v` -> `--v1, --v2, --v3`).
    - if 0 match -> POSITIONAL (unknown option, will end up in extras). `---k` falls here.

  Because ambiguity is raised inside this pass, and the pass short-circuits at the first bare "--", an ambiguous token located AFTER the first "--" NEVER produces an ambiguity error. An ambiguous token BEFORE the "--" still does, and that error wins over every other error (required, unrecognized, expected-one-argument, and even -h/--help: `--help --k` and `-h --k` both print the ambiguity error and exit 2 rather than printing help).

VALUE CONSUMPTION: a token classed DASHDASH is not consumable as an option's value, and it also blocks reaching past it. So if an option requiring one argument is immediately followed by a DASHDASH token, emit
  `test8_executable: error: argument <optstring>: expected one argument`, rc=2
(e.g. `--k1 -- --k` -> `argument --k1: expected one argument`; `--k1 a --v1 -- --k2 b ...` -> `argument --v1: expected one argument`). The only way to give an option the literal value "--" is `--k1=--`, which succeeds and yields `bidict({'--': 1, ...})`.

FATE OF "--" ITSELF: this parser declares no positional arguments, so a DASHDASH token is never absorbed/stripped. Every DASHDASH token, plus every token after the first one, goes into the leftovers list. Second and later "--" tokens are plain POSITIONALs and also land there.

ERROR PRECEDENCE (highest to lowest), all with rc=2 and all preceded by the single usage line
`usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3`:
  1. ambiguous option (from Pass 1, tokens before the first "--" only)
  2. argument <opt>: expected one argument / invalid int value
  3. the following arguments are required: <missing, declaration order, joined ", ">
  4. unrecognized arguments: <leftovers in original argv order, joined by a single " ">
Note 3 fully suppresses 4 (`--k1 x -- --k` prints only `the following arguments are required: --v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3`).

LEFTOVER FORMATTING: leftovers are joined with a single space, with no quoting or escaping. An empty-string leftover therefore yields a trailing space: `test8_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: -- ` (byte-verified). "--" appears literally in the list: `unrecognized arguments: --`, `unrecognized arguments: -- --k`, `unrecognized arguments: -- -- --k`, `unrecognized arguments: -- extra1 extra2`.

CONSEQUENCE FOR HELP: `-h` and `--help` after a "--" are inert POSITIONALs. `-- -h` -> required-args error rc=2; `<all 6 args> -- -h` -> `unrecognized arguments: -- -h` rc=2. Help text is never printed in either case. There is no argv containing a bare "--" that exits 0.

result.implementationNotes:
LOCALE: Hardcode every message in English, unconditionally. Do not read LANG, LANGUAGE, LC_ALL, LC_MESSAGES, LC_CTYPE, or TEXTDOMAINDIR at all. 13 locale/gettext configurations were probed against 5 distinct output paths (missing-args, -h help, invalid-int, unrecognized-args, bidict ValueDuplicationError traceback) — every combination produced byte-identical output. The frozen bundle contains no .mo catalogs (a `strings` scan of /workspace/dataset/test8_executable finds only a stray "*M.MO" fragment and the token "gettext)", plus libpython3.12.so.1.0; no locale/share directory paths), so argparse's gettext lookups always fall through to the msgid. Adding locale plumbing to the port would be dead code.

ENCODING: Always emit raw UTF-8 on both stdout and stderr. PYTHONIOENCODING (tested =ascii and =latin-1), PYTHONUTF8=0, and PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 are all ignored by the frozen runtime. repr() of a str does not escape non-ASCII: `bidict({'é': 1, 'ü✓': 2, 'c': 3})` is written as literal UTF-8 bytes, never \uXXXX. Node's default process.stdout.write(str) UTF-8 behavior matches exactly; add no encoding conditional.

INT PARSING (reimplement Python int(str); do NOT use Number()/parseInt):
1. Strip leading and trailing whitespace only (' 7 ' -> 7). Internal whitespace is an error.
2. Optional single leading '+' or '-' (negatives already known to work, e.g. --v1 -5).
3. Digits may be ANY Unicode decimal-digit (Nd) character: Arabic-Indic ١٢٣ -> 123, fullwidth １２３ -> 123. Map each to its numeric value; printed output is always ASCII digits.
4. Underscores allowed ONLY between two digits (PEP 515): '1_0' -> 10 OK; '_1' -> error; by the same rule '1_' and '1__0' are errors.
5. No thousands separators and no locale decimal comma: '1,000' and '1 000' are errors.
6. On failure write to stderr: the usage line, then `test8_executable: error: argument --vN: invalid int value: '<token>'`, where <token> is the raw argv token wrapped in single quotes (Python repr of the str); exit rc=2.

HELP: `-h`/`--help` writes the help block to STDOUT (stderr empty) and exits rc=0. Header is `options:` (not `optional arguments:`), preceded by a blank line after the usage line.

ABBREVIATION: long-option prefix matching is enabled. Unique prefixes resolve; ambiguous ones produce `test8_executable: error: ambiguous option: --k could match --k1, --k2, --k3` (candidates in argument-declaration order, joined by ", "), rc=2, after the usage line.

PYI TRAILER: the runtime-error trailer is `[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!` on stderr — <pid> is the real process id and changes every run (5580/5620/5685/5726 observed), so generate it (process.pid) rather than hardcoding.

result.dimension: argparse option-vs-value classification: the negative-number matcher (including the `-.5` empty-integer-part branch), its escape hatches, and how rejected shapes surface as errors

findings.rule: `-.5` (leading '-', NO digit before the dot) IS classified as a value, not an option. This exercises the empty-integer-part branch: the fractional alternative is `^-\d*\.\d+$` with `\d*`, NOT `\d+`. A port using `^-\d+\.\d+$` would wrongly emit `argument --k1: expected one argument` here. Stored verbatim as the string key `'-.5'`. Note stderr is EXACTLY empty (0 bytes).

usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3
test8_executable: error: argument --v1: invalid int value: '-.5'
findings.rule: Because `-.5` passes the option/value classifier, it is CONSUMED as --v1's argument and then reaches type=int, which fails. So the error is `invalid int value: '-.5'` (rc=2), NOT `expected one argument`. Classification happens strictly before type coercion — these are two separate failure modes and the port must not conflate them.

`--k1=-5-` yields key `'-5-'`, rc=0 — the only way to feed an option-like string to a str option.

ESCAPE HATCH 2 — any token CONTAINING a literal space (0x20) is treated as a value even if it starts with '-' and is not numeric. `'-e f'` also succeeds -> key `'-e f'`. So the classifier has a `if ' ' in token: return value` rule AFTER the negative-number check.
ESCAPE HATCH 3 — a bare `-` (length exactly 1) is a value, giving key `'-'`, rc=0. Length-1 check precedes the numeric matcher.

prefix_chars is '-' only: tokens starting with '+' (or any non-'-' char) are values immediately, no regex needed. Key `'+5'`.

findings.rule: `\d` in the matcher is UNICODE-aware: `-٥` is accepted as a value. A JS port must use /^-[\p{Nd}]+$|^-[\p{Nd}]*\.[\p{Nd}]+$/u, since JS `\d` is ASCII-only and would misclassify this as an option. Also confirms repr() emits printable non-ASCII literally (raw UTF-8 bytes 2D D9 A5), it does NOT escape to ٥.
int() likewise accepts Unicode Nd digits: int('-٥') == -5, rc=0. The port's int parser must map Unicode decimal digits to their values, not just [0-9].
The fractional alternative is Unicode-aware too: `-٥.٥` accepted as a value (the '.' must still be an ASCII U+002E full stop).

findings.rule: A `--` separator is NOT an escape hatch for option arguments: `--` is swallowed as the end-of-options marker, --k1 is left with no argument -> `argument --k1: expected one argument`, rc=2. Only the `--k1=VALUE` form works for option-like values.

result.implementationNotes:
CLASSIFIER (must run per-argv-token, before any type coercion). Implement `looksLikeOption(tok)` returning false (i.e. token is a VALUE) when ANY of these hold, checked IN THIS ORDER:

1. tok === ''                      -> VALUE   (verified: `--k1 ''` -> key '')
2. tok[0] !== '-'                  -> VALUE   (prefix_chars is '-' only; verified `+5`, ' -5 ')
3. tok is an exact known option string ('-h', '--help', '--k1', '--v1', '--k2', '--v2', '--k3', '--v3') -> OPTION
4. tok.length === 1 (i.e. tok === '-') -> VALUE   (verified: key '-')
5. tok contains '=' and the part before the first '=' is a known option string -> OPTION with inline value = everything after that first '=' (NO classification applied to the value; verified `--k1=-5-`, `--v1=-5-`, `--v1=-5_0`)
6. tok is an unambiguous prefix abbreviation of a known option -> OPTION
7. NEGATIVE-NUMBER MATCHER: if /^-[\p{Nd}]+$/u.test(tok) || /^-[\p{Nd}]*\.[\p{Nd}]+$/u.test(tok) -> VALUE
   - MUST be `[\p{Nd}]*` (zero-or-more) in the fractional alternative so `-.5`, `-.0` are VALUES.
   - MUST require `[\p{Nd}]+` after the '.', so `-.` and `-5.` are OPTIONS.
   - MUST be fully anchored, so `-.5.5` is an OPTION.
   - No exponent support: `-5e3`, `-.5e1` are OPTIONS.
   - No underscores: `-5_0` is an OPTION.
   - Exactly one leading '-': `--5` is an OPTION.
   - Use the /u flag with \p{Nd}, NOT JS `\d` — Python's `\d` matches Unicode decimal digits, verified with U+0665 (`-٥`, `-٥.٥` both VALUES).
   (This branch is only taken because no option string in this program looks like a negative number; that condition is statically true here.)
8. tok.includes(' ')               -> VALUE   (verified `-5 x`, `-e f`)
9. otherwise                       -> OPTION (unknown/option-like)

`--` as a standalone token is consumed as the end-of-options marker and is NEVER available as an option's argument (verified `--k1 -- -5-` fails).

FAILURE MODES (mutually exclusive, both rc=2, both print the usage line first):
- Classifier says OPTION where a value was needed:
  `usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3\n`
  `test8_executable: error: argument <OPT>: expected one argument\n`
  The offending token text is NOT included.
- Classifier says VALUE but int() fails:
  same usage line, then
  `test8_executable: error: argument <OPT>: invalid int value: '<tok>'\n`
  The token is wrapped in Python-repr single quotes.
Both go entirely to stderr; stdout is empty (0 bytes).

INT COERCION (only reached for tokens the classifier passed):
- Strip leading/trailing whitespace (verified `' -5 '` -> -5).
- Optional leading '+'/'-'.
- Allow single '_' separators between digits (verified `--v1=-5_0` -> -50).
- Allow Unicode Nd digits, mapping each to its numeric value (verified `-٥` -> -5).
- Strip leading zeros, decimal only, no octal/hex interpretation (verified `-007` -> -7).
- Reject anything else (dots, exponents, trailing junk) -> `invalid int value` path.

OUTPUT: keys/values are stored and printed exactly as given, with no normalization of the key string. repr() emits printable non-ASCII characters literally as UTF-8 (no \\u escaping) — verified `bidict({'-٥': 1, 'b': 2, 'c': 3})`. Empty-string key reprs as `''`. Every successful run prints exactly 5 lines to stdout, each terminated by a single '\n', and 0 bytes to stderr.

result.implementationNotes:
TERMINAL WIDTH RESOLUTION (implements Python shutil.get_terminal_size() + argparse HelpFormatter width):

1. Read process.env.COLUMNS.
2. If absent -> columns = 80. Else try to parse it with PYTHON int() semantics:
   - Strip leading/trailing Unicode whitespace (space, \t, \n, \r, \v, \f, U+00A0, U+2002, and the rest of the Python str.strip() set). Verified: '  40  ', '\t40\t', '\v40', '\f40', ' 40', ' 40' all -> 40.
   - Accept optional single leading '+' or '-' immediately followed by digits (no space between sign and digits: '- 40' FAILS).
   - Accept decimal digits with optional single '_' separators between digits (PEP 515): '4_0' -> 40.
   - Leading zeros are DECIMAL: '040' -> 40 (not 32).
   - Unicode Nd decimal digits are accepted: '٤٠' -> 40, '４０' -> 40.
   - Arbitrary precision: a 23-digit value parses fine, no overflow.
   - REJECT everything else -> parse failure: '' (empty), ' ' (whitespace only), '0x50', '1e2', '40.0', 'abc', '40abc', '4 0', '- 40', '40\n50'.
   Recommended JS: trim, then test /^[+-]?[0-9](_?[0-9])*$/ (after optionally normalizing Nd digits), then BigInt/Number it. Do NOT use parseInt (accepts '40abc') or Number (accepts '40.0', '1e2', '0x50').
3. If parse FAILED OR the parsed value <= 0 -> columns = 80. (Both branches collapse to 80 because stdout/stderr are not a tty in the harness; treat 80 as the unconditional fallback.) This is the gap: `Number(COLUMNS) || 80` gets 0 right but -5/-1/-0/huge-negative wrong.
4. text_width = columns - 2. (So COLUMNS=80 -> 78; COLUMNS=78 -> 76.)

USAGE BLOCK FORMATTING (argparse _format_usage):
prefix = 'usage: ' (7 chars). prog = 'test8_executable' (16 chars).
Atomized parts for this program, in order (regex \(.*?\)+(?=\s|$) | \[.*?\]+(?=\s|$) | \S+ applied to the formatted optionals string):
  ['[-h]','--k1','K1','--v1','V1','--k2','K2','--v2','V2','--k3','K3','--v3','V3']
Full single-line usage = 'usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3' = exactly 76 chars.

A) If 76 <= text_width (i.e. COLUMNS >= 78, or fallback 80): emit that one 76-char line. All COLUMNS >= 78 are byte-identical.
B) Else wrap. Choose indent style:
   - If 23 <= 0.75 * text_width  (23 = len(prefix)+len(prog); use REAL float math, not integer division) -> HANGING style: indent = 24 spaces (7+16+1). First emitted line is 'usage: test8_executable' followed by as many atoms as fit; continuation lines get the 24-space indent. Threshold: text_width >= 31, i.e. COLUMNS >= 33.
   - Else -> SHORT style: indent = 7 spaces. Line 1 is exactly 'usage: test8_executable' (prog alone, no atoms appended). All atom lines follow with a 7-space indent. Applies to COLUMNS <= 32.
   Greedy packer (both styles): line_len starts at len(indent)-1 for indent-led groups, or len(prefix)-1 for the prefix-led first group in HANGING style. For each atom: if line_len + 1 + len(atom) > text_width AND the current line is non-empty, flush (indent + atoms.join(' ')) and reset line_len to len(indent)-1; then push atom and line_len += 1 + len(atom). Flush remainder at the end. In HANGING style the first flushed line has the indent replaced by the prefix.
   SHORT style extra step (matters here): first pack ALL atoms; if that yields more than 1 line, re-pack and prepend prog as its own line — which is why prog is always alone on line 1 in the SHORT style.
   Saturation: COLUMNS 1..15 (text_width <= 13) all yield the same 14-line block (prog + 13 single-atom lines, 7-space indent). Nothing gets narrower than that; no atom is ever hyphenated or split.

result.dimension: argparse token-level surfaces: `--opt=value` equals form, `--` handling, dedupe across syntaxes, abbreviation/ambiguity, int() coercion, and -h precedence

findings.rule: For a token starting with `--`, split on the FIRST '=' only: everything before is the option name, everything after (even if it contains more '=') is the raw value. Key becomes 'a=b'.
Confirms split-on-first-equals is not greedy and not repeated: value = 'a=b=c'.
`--k1==a` -> value '=a'. The first '=' is the delimiter; a second immediately-following '=' is part of the value.
`--k1=` yields the EMPTY STRING as the key (not an error, not a missing value). Empty string is a legal bidict key and reprs as ''.
The equals form is the ONLY way to pass '--' as a key value; it reprs as '--'. No special-casing of the value after '='.

usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3
test8_executable: error: argument --k1: expected one argument
findings.rule: A standalone `--` is NEVER consumed as an option's value. When `--` immediately follows an option that needs an argument, it is treated as the options-terminator, so the option is left value-less -> `argument <opt>: expected one argument`, rc=2.

Equals form and space form write the SAME dest slot; repeats are allowed (no error) and LAST occurrence wins. k1='b'.
Order-symmetric: space form then equals form also yields last-wins ('b'). Dedupe is purely positional/left-to-right, independent of syntax.

result.implementationNotes:
TOKENIZER / OPTION MATCHING (implement as a left-to-right single pass over argv):

Option table (declaration order matters for messages): -h/--help (flag), --k1(str), --v1(int), --k2(str), --v2(int), --k3(str), --v3(int). All six k/v options are `required`. Matching is case-sensitive.

1. Classify each token:
   - Exactly `--` => OPTIONS TERMINATOR. Set a flag: from here on, every remaining token (including `-h` and `--anything`) is a non-option "extra". CRITICAL: the `--` token itself is NOT removed; push it into the extras list too. Multiple `--` are each retained.
   - Starts with `--`: if it contains '=', split at the FIRST '=' only -> (name, explicitValue) where explicitValue may be '' and may itself contain '=' or leading '-' or be '--'. Otherwise name = whole token, value comes from the NEXT token.
   - Starts with single `-` (and is not exactly `-`): short option. Only `-h` exists.
   - Otherwise: a plain value / extra.
2. Long-option name resolution with PREFIX ABBREVIATION over the 7 long names ['--help','--k1','--v1','--k2','--v2','--k3','--v3']:
   - exact match wins;
   - else collect all names starting with the given prefix. Exactly 1 => use it. >1 => fatal: `ambiguous option: <given> could match <c1>, <c2>, ...` (candidates in declaration order, ', ' separated), rc=2. 0 => UNKNOWN: push the token (and, for the space form, do NOT eagerly consume the following token as its value — the following token also ends up as an extra) into extras and KEEP SCANNING (do not abort; a later -h must still fire).
   - `---` and `---anything` fall into the UNKNOWN bucket (a 3-dash token is not an abbreviation of `--`).
3. -h/--help (or any unambiguous prefix such as `--he`) fires THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED: print the help block to stdout, exit 0, skipping all remaining validation (bad ints, missing required, extras). But it never fires if it appears after a `--` terminator.
4. Value acquisition for the space form (`--k1 X`): consume the next token X as the value ONLY IF X is a legal value. X is NOT a legal value (=> fatal `argument <--opt>: expected one argument`, rc=2) when:
      X is absent (end of argv), OR X is exactly `--`, OR (X starts with '-' AND X !== '-' AND X contains no ' ' AND X does not match /^-\d+$/ and does not match /^-\d*\.\d+$/).
   So `-5` and `-5.5` and `-x y` and `-` ARE legal values; `-x`, `-x_y`, `--5`, `-_5`, `--anything`, `--` are NOT.
   The equals form (`--k1=X`) bypasses this entirely: X is always taken literally, including '', '--', '-x', '=a'.
5. DEDUPE: equals and space forms write the same slot. Repeats are legal; LAST occurrence wins, in pure left-to-right order, regardless of syntax or interleaving. Only the final value is ever used, so values overwritten earlier never participate in bidict duplicate checks.

ERROR PRECEDENCE (exactly one message printed; each error prints the usage line then `test8_executable: error: <msg>`; all to stderr; rc=2):
  a) ambiguous option / expected one argument / invalid int value -> raised immediately when reached during the scan (whichever comes first positionally).
  b) after the scan completes: MISSING REQUIRED first -> `the following arguments are required: <names in declaration order, ', ' separated>` (subset only, e.g. `--v1, --k2, --v2, --k3, --v3`).
  c) only if nothing is missing: `unrecognized arguments: <extras joined by single spaces, original order, verbatim including any '--'>`.

USAGE LINE (byte-exact, printed before every error, and as the first line of help):
`usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3`

HELP BLOCK (stdout, rc=0), byte-exact, trailing newline after the last line:
```
usage: test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --k1 K1
  --v1 V1
  --k2 K2
  --v2 V2
  --k3 K3
  --v3 V3
```
(blank line after usage; section header `options:`; two-space indent; `-h, --help` then two spaces then the help text; the six bare option lines have no help text.)

int() COERCION (for --v1/--v2/--v3) — implement as a custom parser, NOT parseInt/Number:
  - Strip leading/trailing Unicode whitespace (space, \t, \n, \r, \f, \v, and Unicode space separators).
  - Optional single leading '+' or '-'.
  - Then one or more Unicode decimal digits (category Nd — Arabic-Indic '١٢' -> 12 must work), with single '_' separators allowed only BETWEEN digits.
  - Reject: empty/whitespace-only, '_1', '1_', '1__0', '0x10', '5.0', '1 2', '+-5', 'inf', 'nan', '=5', ''.
  - On reject: `argument <--vN>: invalid int value: '<raw arg exactly as received, incl. whitespace and raw UTF-8 bytes>'` — the option name is the actual one encountered, so this is per-option.
  - Result is ARBITRARY PRECISION -> use BigInt. Canonicalize on output: '+5'->5, '007'->7, '-0'->0, '1_000_000'->1000000, and 9999999999999999999999 must print all 22 digits with no exponent and no 'n' suffix.

KEY (str) OPTIONS: no validation at all. Legal keys observed include '', '--', 'a=b', 'a=b=c', '=a', '-5', '-5.5', '-x' (via '='), '-x y'. All repr with single quotes as-is.

result.dimension: Short/long `-h`/`--help` token recognition: single-dash cluster peeling, `=`-attached explicit arguments (including the empty-string form), abbreviation matching, and precedence of help vs. other parse errors

result.implementationNotes:
Implement argparse's exact single-dash cluster algorithm. Only two option strings are registered: '-h' and '--help' (plus the long value-taking '--k1/--v1/--k2/--v2/--k3/--v3'). Prefix char set is {'-'}. TOKEN CLASSIFICATION (left-to-right over argv; a standalone '--' switches everything after it to positional): 1. Empty token '' or token not starting with '-' -> positional. 2. Token exactly '-' (length 1) -> positional. 3. Token exactly '-h' or '--help' -> HELP, no explicit arg. 4. Token starts with '--': split at FIRST '=' into (left, payload) — payload is null if no '='. If left is a non-empty prefix of '--help' (i.e. '--h', '--he', '--hel', '--help'; abbreviation is enabled) -> HELP action with that payload. (Other '--' prefixes match the k/v options or are ambiguous/unknown — out of scope here.) 5. Token starts with '-' and token[1] != '-': let head = token[0:2], tail = token[2:]. - If head != '-h' -> UNKNOWN OPTION: the ENTIRE token verbatim goes to the extras list (never help, never split). - If head == '-h' -> HELP action with (sep, explicit) computed as: if tail starts with '=' then sep='=', explicit=tail[1:]; else sep='', explicit=tail (explicit is null when tail is empty). HELP-ACTION CONSUMPTION LOOP (for a single-dash '-h...' token; '-h' takes 0 arguments): queuedHelp = false loop: if explicit is null -> queuedHelp = true; FIRE if explicit == '' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit('') // e.g. '-h=' if sep == '=' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(explicit) // e.g. '-h=x', '-hh=x' if explicit[0] == '-' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(explicit) // e.g. '-h-', '-h-x', '-h--k1', '-hh--' // otherwise peel one char and continue queuedHelp = true next = '-' + explicit[0]; rest = explicit[1:] if next == '-h': if rest == '' -> FIRE if rest[0] == '=' -> sep='='; explicit=rest[1:]; continue else -> sep=''; explicit=rest; continue else: extras.push('-' + explicit) // whole remaining cluster, unreported because help fires FIRE FIRE = print the 193-byte help text to stdout and exit(0) immediately. For the LONG form (case 4) there is no peeling: if payload is null -> FIRE; else -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(payload) (payload may be ''). NET OBSERVABLE RULE for single-dash tokens: with R = token[2:] after a leading '-h', R == '' -> help, rc 0 R starts with '=' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(R[1:]) (empty -> '') R[0] == '-' -> ERROR ignoredExplicit(R) R[0] not in {'-','=','h'} -> help, rc 0 (rest silently discarded) R[0] == 'h' -> recurse with token = '-' + R Help is printed at most ONCE no matter how many 'h's. result.implementationNotes:
STDOUT-WRITE-FAILURE RULES A PORTER MUST IMPLEMENT (Node.js)

Model stdout as an 8192-byte block-buffered stream whenever stdout is not a TTY. Maintain `pending` = bytes accumulated. For each `print(s)` push `s + "\n"`:
  - Let n = byte length of the chunk (UTF-8).
  - If n >= 8192: write it directly to fd 1 (buffer must be empty at that point, since it is flushed first in practice for this program's access pattern).
  - Else: pending += n; if pending >= 8192, flush the buffer to fd 1 now, then hold the chunk.
  The FIRST operation whose write/flush hits a failing fd is where the exception is raised. Verified boundary: exactly 8192 (>= not >). PYTHONUNBUFFERED is ignored.

Byte lengths for this program with keys K1,K2,K3 and values V1,V2,V3:
  L1 = len("bidict({" + repr-pairs + "})") + 1
  L2 = len(String(V1)) + 1
  L3 = len(String(K2)) + 1   (value of b.inv[V2])
  L4 = len(String(K3)) + 1   (value of b.inv[V3])
  L5 = len(repr after b[K1]=999) + 1
For single-char K2/K3 and a K1 of length L: L1 = L+32, L2=L3=L4=2, L5 = L+34.

CASE 1 - stdout open but every write fails (e.g. /dev/full), and the whole run's output fits without any mid-run flush (the ordinary 5-short-line run):
  exit code 0. stdout: nothing. stderr, exactly:
    "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File \"<string>\", line 1, in <module>\nOSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device\nException ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' mode='w' encoding='utf-8'>\nOSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device\n"
  No "[PYI-...]" line. The frame is literally `<string>`, line 1, with no source-text line.

CASE 2 - a write/flush fails during a print (output large enough to force a mid-run flush):
  exit code 1. stderr, exactly:
    "Traceback (most recent call last):\n  File \"test8.py\", line <N>, in <module>\n    <SOURCE TEXT>\nOSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device\n[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!\n"
  where <N>/<SOURCE TEXT> come from this map (4-space indent on the source line, no caret line for print frames):
    18 -> "print(b)"                (first repr)
    21 -> "print(b[args.k1])"
    22 -> "print(b.inv[args.v2])"
    23 -> "print(b.inv[args.v3])"
    27 -> "print(b)"                (final repr)
  NO "Exception ignored in:" block in this case.

CASE 3 - bidict exception AND non-empty unflushable buffer: print the normal script traceback + "[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test8' due to unhandled exception!\n" FIRST, then append the CASE-1 two-block text ("<string>" traceback + "Exception ignored in:"). exit code 1. CASE 6 - argparse paths are immune to stdout state EXCEPT --help:

result.implementationNotes:
WIDTH RESOLUTION (implement exactly, in this order):

1. raw = process.env.COLUMNS. If raw is defined, parse with Python int() semantics: trim ASCII whitespace (space, \t, \n, \r, \v, \f); accept /^[+-]?\d+(_\d+)*$/ (optional sign, underscore digit separators allowed); strip underscores and Number() it. On any parse failure -> cols = 0. Do NOT use parseInt (it would accept '40.5' and '0x28', both of which the reference REJECTS).
2. If cols <= 0: if process.stdout.isTTY and process.stdout.columns is a positive integer -> cols = process.stdout.columns. Use STDOUT only — never stderr, and never process.stderr.columns. Verified: stdout->file + stderr->40-col tty yields 80.
3. If still <= 0 (no tty, or tty reports nothing) -> cols = 80.
4. width = cols - 2. (May go negative for tiny cols; the algorithms below still work with a negative width.)

Nothing else in the program depends on width: the five bidict output lines, all tracebacks, and the trailing '[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] ...' line are emitted verbatim regardless.

USAGE BLOCK ('usage: ' + wrapped) — argparse HelpFormatter._format_usage:
  prefix = 'usage: ' (len 7); prog = 'test8_executable' (len 16).
  full_usage = 'test8_executable [-h] --k1 K1 --v1 V1 --k2 K2 --v2 V2 --k3 K3 --v3 V3' (69 chars; 'usage: ' + that = 76).
  text_width = width - 0.
  If 7 + 69 <= text_width (i.e. cols >= 78): emit one line 'usage: <full_usage>\n'. Done.
  Else split into parts: optionals = ['[-h]', '--k1 K1', '--v1 V1', '--k2 K2', '--v2 V2', '--k3 K3', '--v3 V3']; positionals = [].
  get_lines(parts, indent, prefix?):
      line = []; line_len = (prefix ? prefix.length : indent.length) - 1
      for part of parts:
          if line_len + 1 + part.length > text_width && line.length > 0:
              push(indent + line.join(' ')); line = []; line_len = indent.length - 1
          line.push(part); line_len += 1 + part.length
      if line.length: push(indent + line.join(' '))
      if prefix: lines[0] = lines[0].slice(indent.length)   // strip indent from first line
      return lines
  Branch on whether prog fits on line 1:
      if 7 + 16 <= 0.75 * text_width   (true iff text_width >= 30.667, i.e. cols >= 33):
          indent = ' '.repeat(7 + 16 + 1) = 24 spaces
          lines = get_lines([prog, ...optionals], indent, prefix)
      else:
          indent = ' '.repeat(7) = 7 spaces
          lines = get_lines(optionals, indent)          // no prefix arg
          lines = [prog, ...lines]                       // prog alone on its own line
      result = prefix + lines.join('\n') + '\n'   (i.e. 'usage: ' prepended; in the second branch that makes line 1 'usage: test8_executable')
  When a single part is longer than the available room it is still emitted alone on its line (see cols=15: '--k1' and 'K1' end up on separate lines because argparse's part regex splits an option from its metavar when the option group itself must break).
  Reference wrap points to test against: cols 15,20,25,30,31,32,33,40,50,60 — exact expected bytes are in the findings above.

HELP BLOCK (-h, rc=0), after the usage block, then '\n' then 'options:\n':
  action_max_length = 12   (2-space indent + len('-h, --help')); the metavar-only actions give 2+7=9.
  max_help_position = min(24, max(width - 20, 4))
  help_position     = min(action_max_length + 2, max_help_position) = min(14, max_help_position)
  action_width      = help_position - 2 /*current_indent*/ - 2
  help_width        = max(width - help_position, 11)
  For '-h, --help' (help text 'show this help message and exit'):
      if 10 <= action_width  (equivalently help_position === 14, equivalently width >= 34, equivalently cols >= 36):
          first line = '  -h, --help' padded with spaces to column help_position (=14) + helpLines[0]
          subsequent lines = ' '.repeat(14) + line
      else:
          emit '  -h, --help\n' then every help line as ' '.repeat(help_position) + line
      helpLines = greedy word-wrap of 'show this help message and exit' to help_width.
  For --k1..--v3 (no help text): always exactly '  --k1 K1\n', '  --v1 V1\n', ... with no padding, at every width.
  Verified indents: cols 5/10/12/20/25 -> 4; cols 30 -> 8; 33 -> 11; 34 -> 12; 35 -> 13; 36+ -> inline at 14.

ERROR LINE: 'test8_executable: error: <message>\n' is written to stderr with NO wrapping ever, after the (wrapped) usage block; rc=2.
